prompt: A sculptor's studio at night, single powerful spotlight mounted at a precise angle. Center of the scene: a complex, dense wire sculpture on a low pedestal — hundreds of wire strands intersecting at various angles, intricate and almost impossible to read as a coherent shape from any viewpoint in 3D, the internal structure obscured by its own complexity. Behind it on the plain white studio wall, the spotlight casts a sharp, clean shadow — and that shadow is immediately and clearly readable as a bird in flight, wings outstretched, form unmistakable. The 3D object is chaos; the 2D projection is clarity. The sculpture and its shadow are both in focus. The studio is physically real — wooden floors, paint-stained surfaces, other works in the background. No text. No labels. No annotations. Photorealistic large-format photography, high contrast between the complex sculpture and the clean shadow, warm spotlight against cool ambient studio light
metaphor: A chaotic 3D wire sculpture becomes a clear bird when projected as a 2D shadow, preserving the essential structure in fewer dimensions.
